value.rationale: A complete distance-refined ordered-pair extension spectrum is a natural next invariant after unary Katětov counts. The theorem isolates three sharply different limiting laws as the old equilateral distance changes: two nondegenerate three-distance laws and one concentration at distance 2. All n and every base distance in the three-letter ambient alphabet are covered. The mean number of allowed mutual distances is also determined, distinguishing unary-type counts from complete pair-type counts; no general downstream theorem is claimed.
